Alaska.Ai — The Stack Draft

2026-06-16 · branch claude/linkedin-stack-2026-06-16
No defensible target this cycle. The seven-point anti-confabulation gate cleared zero mechanisms at both the 14-day window (June 2–16) and the 21-day broadening retry (May 26–June 16). No post was drafted and no image was rendered. This is the third consecutive no-target run (June 12, June 15, June 16). The bar was not lowered.

What the scouts found

Four category scouts (facilities, vehicles, capital/sovereignty, regulatory) ran in parallel. Together they surfaced five candidate mechanisms with in-window or near-window news triggers. The mapper applied all seven gates to each. None survived.

Dropped mechanisms

MechanismCategoryGate failures
Quintillion Nome-Homer Express FWS Compatibility Determination Stack facilities Gate 1 FAIL: The sole trigger source was fws.gov/story — the agency’s own page. No independent news outlet (ADN, Alaska Public Media, KTOO, Alaska Beacon) covered the FWS notice within June 2–16.

Gate 5 FAIL: 50 CFR 26.41, fetched from law.cornell.edu, explicitly requires BOTH the Refuge Manager’s signature AND the Regional Chief’s concurrence signature on every Compatibility Determination. Two required signatories — the scout’s argument that 16 U.S.C. 668dd makes this a single-actor process is directly contradicted by the implementing regulation. Prior drop from June 7–15 runs confirmed by fetched primary source.
SBA 8(a) ANC Entity-Owned Statutory Immunity Stack capital_sovereignty Gate 4 FAIL: Neither the Alaska Public Media article (June 12), the ADN article (June 11), nor the KNBA article (June 15) mentions any AI sector consequence, any ANC AI subsidiary, or any direct Alaska AI impact. The connection to Alaska AI is purely inferential (“ANC subsidiaries include IT firms that do AI work”) — not a concrete, documentable consequence with sector + decision/risk + named actor + timeframe.

Gate 7 FAIL: The “ANC 8(a) Sole-Source Federal Contracting Pipeline” was anatomized May 25. The “immunity architecture” framing maps the same statute (15 U.S.C. § 637(a)(13)), same SBA program structure, same SBA Administrator apex, same ANC entity-owned exemption. Re-mapping the same layer chain under a different analytical frame is prohibited.
AETC BOS MAC IDIQ (FA300226D000X) vehicles Gate 4 FAIL: All 11 work locations are lower-48 Air Force installations (Oklahoma, Texas, Alabama, Mississippi, Arizona, New Mexico). The posited Alaska AI consequence — ANC firms accumulating past performance that feeds into future Alaska competition — is inferential, not concrete.

Gate 5 FAIL: No individual Source Selection Authority named in any fetched source. Only “338th Enterprise Sourcing Squadron” as an organizational unit. An org unit without a named individual does not satisfy the single-actor binary decision requirement.
Greensparc SEAPA Stranded-Hydro Edge Data Center Siting Stack facilities Gate 5 FAIL: The Wrangell Borough Assembly is a multi-member vote body. Mayor Gilbert’s stated intent to deny the lease is advisory — the formal institutional decision is the full Assembly vote. Multi-member assembly vote = committee, not chokepoint.
GCI-Quintillion SCL Transfer (FCC Cable Landing License) regulatory Gate 1 FAIL: GCI-Quintillion acquisition announced April 22, 2026 — 54 days outside the 21-day broadened window (May 26 start). No in-window independent article specifically discusses the FCC cable landing license transfer mechanism.

Gate 3 FAIL: The SCL-T/C application has not been filed with the FCC as of June 16, 2026. The application document does not exist and cannot be cited as a primary source for any layer.

Pattern note

  • This is the third consecutive no-target run (June 12, June 15, June 16). Prior no-target runs: June 11, June 12, June 15.
  • The Quintillion FWS Compatibility Determination Stack has now been dropped across multiple runs for the same Gate 5 failure (50 CFR 26.41 dual-signature requirement). This mechanism may clear if an independent outlet covers the FWS notice before the June 19 public comment deadline.
  • The GCI-Quintillion SCL transfer mechanism becomes eligible for Gate 1 once an independent news outlet covers the FCC filing specifically. The SCL-T/C application has not yet been filed as of this run.
  • The SBA 8(a) immunity story (June 11–12) is rich news with genuine Alaska impact, but passes neither Gate 4 (no named AI consequence) nor Gate 7 (same layer chain as May 25). A mechanism anchored specifically to an ANC AI subsidiary’s sole-source contract award — with a named technology decision — would clear both gates.
  • The Greensparc/SEAPA stranded-hydro mechanism is the most novel in this window. If the Petersburg variant (private parcel, no assembly vote, single utility director decision) surfaces in an independent outlet, it may clear Gate 5 where the Wrangell version cannot.

Candidates to watch next cycle

  • FWS Quintillion CD notice — public comment closes June 19. If ADN, Alaska Public Media, or KTOO covers it before then, Gate 1 clears. Gate 5 still requires either a single-actor regulatory workaround or a different legal reading of the CD authority.
  • GCI-Quintillion FCC SCL-T/C filing — monitor FCC IBFS for the filing. Once filed, the mechanism has a named TAD Chief (Denise Coca) as the binary actor and a strong Gate 1 trigger in the filing itself (Federal Register public notice).
  • Greensparc Petersburg variant — private parcel at the Ocean Beauty cannery waterfront, single utility director (Steve Harbour, incoming Petersburg Municipal Power & Light Director) as the binary actor. If any independent outlet covers the Petersburg variant, this is a strong facilities candidate.
  • CIRI/OSC Technical Solutions — the capital_sovereignty AI investment stack is well-documented, but the freshest trigger is May 19 (outside the window). Any new contract award or announcement in the June 17–23 window would make this the strongest candidate for the next run.

Editor’s note

  • 14-day window exhausted at zero survivors; broadened to 21 days per protocol.
  • 21-day window also produced zero survivors.
  • No post drafted, no image rendered (no-target case).
  • No deviations from procedure. The anti-confabulation gate held across all five candidates.
  • Consecutive no-target run streak: 3 (June 12, June 15, June 16). This is consistent with a news-environment pattern where most Alaska AI mechanisms surfacing in this window either lack independent editorial coverage or have structurally diffuse chokepoints (multi-member commissions).
